packets.responsibility: Declares the gesture's module-level drag state and the capture-phase `#frame-grid` mousedown listener that arms it: hit-tests the grab zone, computes every bound the drag will be constrained to, snapshots the tail keyframes that will ripple, and dims the source/next-keyframe markers for the drag's duration.
behavior: Section header (4788) plus a 30-line lead-in comment (4789-4817, spanning two topics separated by a blank comment line at 4804): the first block (4789-4803) explains WHY this listener must be capture-phase AND call stopImmediatePropagation() — a held span's visual end has no stored length (always wherever the next real keyframe sits), so grabbing it must intercept before the plain-cell mousedown handler below (next leaf, 5091) can also fire and start an unrelated `_tlDrag` range-select on the same press (mere stopPropagation() did not stop it, since both listeners sit on `#frame-grid` and at-target listeners on one element fire in registration order regardless of capture flag — only stopImmediatePropagation() skips a later sibling); also documents the grab zone as the whole `.fc.span-end` cell (14px wide, ~7px of hit area historically). The second block (4805-4817) explains the trim-not-insert semantics: if a real keyframe borders the span right after it (nextKeyFi), dragging relocates that keyframe's own content (video-editor-style trim) rather than always inserting a new keyframe at the drop point (the pre-fix behavior, which left the original next keyframe in place); with no bordering keyframe, there is nothing to trim, so it falls back to inserting a new keyframe (the only way to shrink an open-ended hold).

`_spanShrink` (4818): module-level var, initial value `{active:false,li:-1,srcFi:-1,maxFi:-1,nextKeyFi:-1,dragMax:-1}` — no `laterKeys` key present in the initial literal (only added by the first arm, 4875).
Listener registration (4819): `document.getElementById('frame-grid').addEventListener('mousedown',function(e){...},true)` — capture phase (third argument `true`).
Arm condition, guard 1 (4820): `if(e.button!==0)return;` — left button only, no modifier-key (shift/ctrl/meta) checks anywhere in this listener.

Arm condition, guard 2/hit-test (4821): `var cell=e.target.closest('.fc.span-end');if(!cell)return;` — the sole hit-test; any mousedown whose event target is not inside a `.fc.span-end` cell falls through to the sibling listener untouched.

v8 comment (4822-4829): documents that the hit zone was progressively widened across earlier passes (7px -> 65% -> the whole cell) because a `.fc.span-end` cell's only useful single-cell action was ever this resize, so claiming the whole cell loses no competing gesture; the matching CSS grab-bar (`.fc.span-end::after`, style.css, out of scope) was resized to match.

Propagation suppression (4830): `e.preventDefault();e.stopPropagation();e.stopImmediatePropagation();` — three calls on one line; per the section comment, stopImmediatePropagation() is the one that actually matters for suppressing the sibling `#frame-grid` mousedown listener (next leaf, 5091).
Coordinate/layer resolution (4831): `var fi=parseInt(cell.dataset.frame),li=parseInt(cell.dataset.layer);` from the grabbed cell's own dataset.

Locked-layer guard (4832-4833): `var ld=state.layers[li];if(ld.locked){showToast(SM.t('toastLayerLocked'));return;}` with an inline comment ('span-end drag is a keyframe edit like any other (feedback #18)') — a locked layer aborts the whole arm sequence: `_spanShrink` is never reassigned, no DOM class is added, and (because stopImmediatePropagation already ran at 4830) the sibling mousedown listener never fires either, so a locked layer's span-end cell is fully inert to this gesture.

srcFi resolution (4834): backward scan `for(var pi=fi;pi>=0;pi--){if(ld.frames[pi].isKeyframe){srcFi=pi;break;}}`, initialized to `fi` — finds the nearest real keyframe at or before the grabbed cell (the span's own start).

nextKeyFi resolution (4835-4836): `-1` unless `ld.frames[fi+1]` exists and `isKeyframe` is true, in which case `nextKeyFi=fi+1` — this is what selects the trim-vs-insert branch everywhere else in the gesture.

dragMax computation (4837-4867, preceded by two comments: a short one at 4837-4840 stating the raw bound, and a 15-line one at 4841-4856 explaining the 2026-07-28 ripple fix — a third occurrence of a bug already fixed for Motion's layer-bar drag and Animation 2D's keyframe-dot drag): if `nextKeyFi>=0` (4858-4866), forward-scans from `nextKeyFi+1` to the end of `ld.frames` tracking `lastKeyInChain` (the LAST keyframe in the tail, 4859-4860), then sets `dragMax=nextKeyFi+((state.totalFrames-1)-lastKeyInChain)` (4865, with an in-source note at 4861-4864 that this bound is relative to `nextKeyFi`, the thing that actually moves, not the grabbed cell's own `fi`, called out as a bug caught before shipping); else (4867) `dragMax=fi` — the pre-existing shrink-only cap, no bordering keyframe to relocate.

laterKeys snapshot (4868-4874, preceded by a 5-line comment at 4868-4872 on why this is captured ONCE here and not recomputed per mousemove tick): `var laterKeys=[];if(nextKeyFi>=0)for(var lki=nextKeyFi+1;lki<ld.frames.length;lki++){if(ld.frames[lki].isKeyframe)laterKeys.push(lki);}` — every keyframe strictly after `nextKeyFi`, in ascending order; empty array when `nextKeyFi<0`.

`_spanShrink` arm write (4875): whole-object replacement (not a partial/field-by-field mutation) — `_spanShrink={active:true,li:li,srcFi:srcFi,maxFi:fi,nextKeyFi:nextKeyFi,dragMax:dragMax,laterKeys:laterKeys};`. Note `maxFi` is assigned the grabbed cell's own `fi` (the span-end cell's frame, i.e. `nextKeyFi-1` when a bordering keyframe exists), distinct from `dragMax` (the actual drag ceiling).

Arm-time DOM feedback (4876-4886, preceded by a 3-line comment at 4876-4878 on why dimmed rather than hidden): `cell.classList.add('tl-outdrag-source-end')` (4879) keeps the original span-end marker visible-but-dimmed as a reference during the drag; a second comment (4880-4882) frames the next block as the trim-path-only counterpart — if `nextKeyFi>=0` (4883-4886), looks up the bordering keyframe's own cell via `document.querySelector('.fc[data-layer="'+li+'"][data-frame="'+nextKeyFi+'"]')` and, if found, adds `tl-outdrag-source-key` to dim its dot too.

This packet performs no `ld.frames[...]`/`isKeyframe`/`strokes` write and calls no `pushUndo`/`saveActiveLayerFrame`/`saveAllLayerFrames`/`loadFrame`/`renderTimeline`/`updateUI` — it only arms in-memory drag state and adds two CSS classes.

HIT_TOLERANCE_PX comment (4891-4901, 11 lines): explains that `Math.floor(x/FC)` alone would put the ambiguous cell boundary exactly at each cell's LEFT edge, which is where a user aiming to drop on frame N naturally releases, so an unadjusted floor silently lands one frame short (feedback quoted verbatim); a few pixels of forward tolerance fixes this without materially changing a deliberate drop several cells earlier, given FC is only ~16px at default zoom.
`var HIT_TOLERANCE_PX=4;` (4902).

Return (4903): `return Math.max(_spanShrink.srcFi+1,Math.min(_spanShrink.dragMax,Math.floor((x+HIT_TOLERANCE_PX)/FC)));` — clamps the tolerance-adjusted floored frame index between a hard floor of `_spanShrink.srcFi+1` (never resolves onto or before the source keyframe) and a hard ceiling of `_spanShrink.dragMax` (the bound computed once at arm time, previous packet).

proposed_behavioral_fixtures.initial_state: A left-button mousedown dispatched at four targets: a `.fc.span-end` cell on an unlocked layer, a `.fc.span-end` cell on a locked layer, a plain `.fc` cell that is not `.span-end`, and a non-`.fc` element inside `#frame-grid`.
proposed_behavioral_fixtures.expected_effects: Only the unlocked `.fc.span-end` case sets `_spanShrink.active=true` and calls `stopImmediatePropagation()`; the locked-layer case calls `showToast` and leaves `_spanShrink.active` false without ever calling `stopImmediatePropagation()`; the other two cases leave `_spanShrink` untouched and let the sibling `#frame-grid` mousedown listener (next leaf) run normally.

proposed_behavioral_fixtures.initial_state: Both the capture-phase span-shrink arm listener (4819) and the bubble-phase sibling mousedown listener (next leaf, 5091) registered on the identical `#frame-grid` element; a mousedown dispatched on a `.fc.span-end` cell.
proposed_behavioral_fixtures.expected_effects: The sibling listener's own body never executes for this event (confirmable by a spy/counter) because `stopImmediatePropagation()` (4830) runs first, in registration/phase order — `_tlDrag.active` remains false/unchanged throughout the gesture.

proposed_behavioral_fixtures.initial_state: A layer with keyframes at frames 10 (grabbed span-end at 14, nextKeyFi=15) and 30 (the sole later keyframe), totalFrames=40.
proposed_behavioral_fixtures.expected_effects: dragMax = nextKeyFi + ((totalFrames-1) - lastKeyInChain) = 15 + (39-30) = 24, NOT `14 + (39-30)=23` — confirming the bound is anchored to nextKeyFi (what moves) and not the grabbed cell's own fi, per the in-source correction comment.

proposed_behavioral_fixtures.initial_state: A pointer x landing exactly on a cell's left edge (the pre-tolerance floor boundary), and separately, pointer positions computed to resolve below srcFi+1 and above dragMax.
proposed_behavioral_fixtures.expected_effects: The left-edge case resolves to the cell the user visually released on (not one frame short) because of the +4px tolerance; out-of-range raw floors are clamped to exactly srcFi+1 (lower) or dragMax (upper), never producing a frame outside that closed interval.

proposed_behavioral_fixtures.initial_state: Two consecutive mousemove events during an active drag, five frames apart in resolved fi.
proposed_behavioral_fixtures.expected_effects: Every `.span-drag-band`/`.span-drag-preview`/`.span-drag-dot-cell` class and every `.km.drag-key-preview` element present after the first event is fully removed before the second event's own band/preview/dot classes and elements are added — no stale marker from the first tick survives into the second.

proposed_behavioral_fixtures.initial_state: A trim drag (nextKeyFi>=0) with the pointer resolving to fi=20 mid-drag.
proposed_behavioral_fixtures.expected_effects: The relocating keyframe's own preview dot (`.km.drag-key-preview`) appears in the `.fc[data-frame=20]` cell (the SAME frame `_spanShrinkFrameAt` will return on mouseup for an unchanged pointer position), not frame 21 — regression guard for the documented 2026-07-28 one-frame-late preview bug.

proposed_behavioral_fixtures.initial_state: A trim drag with two later keyframes in `laterKeys` (origFi=30 and 45), dragged so delta=+3.
proposed_behavioral_fixtures.expected_effects: The ripple preview dots appear at newFi=33 and 48, each classed full/hollow according to `ld.frames[origFi]` (30 and 45's OWN original strokes), not `ld.frames[newFi]` (whatever those target slots currently hold) and not mutated during the preview — `ld.frames` is byte-identical before and after any number of mousemove ticks until mouseup commits.

proposed_behavioral_fixtures.initial_state: Three separate drags, each ended with a mouseup satisfying exactly one of: fi<=srcFi; nextKeyFi>=0 and fi===nextKeyFi; nextKeyFi<0 and fi>=maxFi.
proposed_behavioral_fixtures.expected_effects: In all three cases, `ld.frames` is byte-identical to its pre-drag state, `pushUndo`/`saveAllLayerFrames`/`insertKeyframeAt` are never called, and every preview/dim DOM class and element added during arm/drag is still fully removed by the cleanup sweep (4977-4986) that runs before any cancel check.

proposed_behavioral_fixtures.initial_state: A trim commit with toMove=[15,30] (two keyframes to ripple) and delta=+5, where the target slot for one moving keyframe (20) coincides with the CURRENT (pre-move) position of the other's neighborhood.
proposed_behavioral_fixtures.expected_effects: Every `captured[i].content` is read from `ld.frames` BEFORE any `ld.frames[from]` is blanked (pass 1 completes for all entries before pass 2 writes any `to` slot) — the final `ld.frames` state matches applying the full delta shift atomically, with no entry silently overwritten by another entry's blank-write mid-sequence.

proposed_behavioral_fixtures.initial_state: A trim commit where an interpolated (isInterpolated=true) frame lies strictly between the original nextKeyFi and its post-ripple destination.
proposed_behavioral_fixtures.expected_effects: That interpolated frame's own isInterpolated/strokes content is left completely untouched by the three-pass write (it is not in `toMove`, only real keyframes are) — consistent with the in-source disclosure that tween/arc rekeying is not attempted for this gesture, so the frame becomes orphaned relative to the moved keyframe pair it used to sit between.

proposed_behavioral_fixtures.initial_state: An open-ended-hold drag (nextKeyFi<0) with a valid drop fi < maxFi, on a layer whose target frame is not already a keyframe.
